content.text: In July, the renowned locomotive is scheduled to travel along the route connecting Bridgnorth in Shropshire to Kidderminster in Worcestershire to mark the complete reopening of the heritage railway.

Stuart Nelhams: It's always a special day to be driving steam locomotives but especially to get on one that is considered a national icon. It's become a bit of a pop star, people seem to know the name.

The railway is due to hold a Swinging Sixties weekend on 26 and 27 July and people who miss out on Flying Scotsman tickets have been urged to attend the event where they can travel on other services and will be able to see the world's most famous locomotive in action.
